comment: GS1 coding: DHIS2 natively features parsing of GS1 DataMatrix codes. However, regardless of coding requirements in the Product Catalogue, for stock management only the codes printed on products are relevant and those depend on (international) manufacturers. For the last mile, using manufacturer codes is not practical because not all products feature codes (especially non-sterile medical devices) and because two products from two different manufacturers can be therapeutically equivalent but need to be managed as the same stock entity. Therefore, it is much better to use QR-code labels on shelving which must of course be aligned with the national registry.

public.text: GS1 coding: DHIS2 natively features parsing of GS1 DataMatrix codes. However, regardless of coding requirements in the Product Catalogue, for stock management only the codes printed on products are relevant and those depend on (international) manufacturers. For the last mile, using manufacturer codes is not practical because not all products feature codes (especially non-sterile medical devices) and because two products from two different manufacturers can be therapeutically equivalent but need to be managed as the same stock entity. Therefore, it is much better to use QR-code labels on shelving which must of course be aligned with the national registry.
